ov: About 2,000 species of insects with forceps-like pincers on the tail, found on every continent except Antarctica. Mostly nocturnal, they hide in damp crevices by day and eat a wide mix of plants and insects. Most can fly but rarely do.

why.ac: It hides in damp crevices by day and comes out at night to feed.

rg: Every continent except Antarctica; the common earwig was introduced to North America from Europe in 1907.
df: Mostly scavengers of dead plant and animal matter; the common earwig also eats plants, ripe fruit and small insects.
fx: The hind wings unfold into a shape like a human ear, which may be where the name really comes from.
A mother cleans her eggs to keep fungus off them, and has been seen cleaning wax balls by mistake.
